title: White clover as a living mulch
subtitle: A nitrogen-fixing ground cover that suppresses weeds between taller crops.
excerpt: White clover grown as a living mulch between crop rows fixes atmospheric nitrogen, suppresses weeds, and gives bees something to forage. It can be mown or rolled to suppress it when the main crop needs more space.
sourceNotes: Nitrogen fixation rates from agricultural extension literature. Mowing timing for clover suppression after organic horticultural guidance from Garden Organic.

glossaryTerms.definition: A low-growing plant deliberately sown between taller crops to cover bare soil. A good living mulch suppresses weeds, retains moisture, and (if nitrogen-fixing) adds fertility. It needs managing so it does not compete too strongly with the main crop.

A small swelling on the root of a legume plant where nitrogen-fixing bacteria live. The bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen into a form the plant can use. When the roots die or are cut, some of this nitrogen becomes available in the soil.

content.text: White clover grown between crop rows is a

and keeps the soil covered without the need for mulch materials. It is most useful in orchards, between raised beds, and under taller perennial crops where bare soil is otherwise left open all season.

White clover works well as path cover between raised beds, under fruit trees, and between soft fruit bushes. It also suits the strips between brassica rows on a no-dig bed and any open ground on a new plot before planting begins.

Do not use it as a living mulch directly under or between plants that need a lot of nitrogen, such as leeks, celery, and hungry salad crops. The clover fixes nitrogen from the air, but it also competes for moisture and space with neighbouring shallow-rooted plants.

Sow from March to April or in August to September on raked bare soil. Broadcast the seed thinly. Rake in very lightly; the seed needs contact with soil but not depth. Keep moist until germinated (about 10 to 14 days in spring).

When the main crop is growing strongly and starts to shade out the clover, mow or strim the clover to 5 cm. This checks it for a few weeks and reduces competition. In a no-dig bed, you can use a Dutch hoe to cut along the row edge, keeping the clover from creeping into the crop space.
Let the clover flower once a year if possible. The flowers feed bees. Cut them off before they set seed if you want to prevent the clover spreading further than intended.

attrs.title: Clover as part of the no-dig rotation
attrs.body: On a no-dig bed, let white clover self-establish in a bed after a heavy-feeding crop has been cleared. Leave it for one full season. When you next want to use the bed, cut the clover to the ground, top-dress with compost, and plant straight in. The nitrogen fixed by the root nodules is available in the soil immediately after cutting and helps establish the next crop without any additional feeding.
